title: Customer-facing narrative + Support macros for regional failover automation reliability work
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
- Recent regional degradations highlighted gaps in detection + manual failover decisioning. SRE/Platform are shipping automated, safety-guarded orchestration (progressive failover, safe-to-failover checks, graceful degradation).
- We need a customer-facing narrative that explains what’s improving (and what is not changing) without over-promising “no outages.”
- Support/CS needs updated macros + escalation guidance for (a) controlled failover tests and (b) real incidents while automation is in monitor-only / partial rollout.

Goals
1) Align internal messaging on what we’re building (automation + guardrails) and expected customer-visible behavior.
2) Produce a customer-safe narrative (1-pager + short FAQ) for enterprise assurance conversations.
3) Update Support macros + escalation playbook to reduce confusion during controlled tests and real regional impairment.

Non-goals / guardrails
- Do not promise “instant failover,” “zero downtime,” or “no customer impact.”
- Do not commit to specific thresholds, exact timing windows, or a guaranteed set of regions/models covered on day 1.
- Avoid publishing implementation details that increase attack surface (exact signals, internal endpoints, automation commands).

Key messages (draft)
- What’s changing: We’re improving multi-region resilience by standardizing health signals, automating progressive failover with safety checks, and improving graceful degradation when a region is impaired.
- What this means for customers: During regional issues, we aim to reduce sustained error rates/timeouts by routing traffic away from unhealthy regions sooner and more consistently, while preserving capacity and correctness.
- What’s not changing: Customers may still see brief increased latency, transient errors, or reconnects during regional instability and controlled tests; automation is designed to be conservative and may prefer degraded-but-available behavior over aggressive failover.
- Safety posture: Failover is gated by “safe-to-failover” checks (target capacity/dependency health) and uses progressive ramp with rollback; humans remain in the loop with manual overrides.

Deliverables
A) Customer-facing 1-pager (for enterprise assurance)
- Title: “Multi-region reliability improvements: automated failover + graceful degradation”
- Sections: Overview, What we’re improving, What customers may observe, How we test safely (controlled failovers), How to engage Support during incidents, FAQ.
- Review path: SRE (Sean/Aisha), Platform (Mina/Ethan), Support (Dev), Legal/Comms as-needed.

B) FAQ (short; can be embedded in email follow-ups)
- “Do you automatically fail over between regions?”
- “Will I experience downtime during failover?”
- “How do controlled failover tests work and how will I be notified?”
- “Does this apply to Dedicated/Private deployments?” (Answer: varies by deployment mode and customer configuration; we can discuss architecture options.)
- “What information should I provide when reporting a regional issue?”

C) Support/CS macros + escalation guidance
- Macro: Controlled failover test (pre-announce) — what customers might see; reassurance; where to report issues.
- Macro: During suspected regional degradation — request IDs, timestamps, model/route, region (if known), streaming vs non-streaming, SDK version; confirm mitigations in progress.
- Macro: Post-incident follow-up — summary language focusing on impact and mitigations without exposing sensitive internals; pointer to reliability roadmap at a high level.
- Escalation routing: when to page SRE vs Platform vs Infra; how to tag SUP tickets; expected SLA for initial response during a wide incident.

D) Internal enablement note
- Short internal post for Support/CS + Solutions: “How to talk about automated failover and controlled tests” + do/don’t language.

Proposed ‘do/don’t’ language
- DO: “We’re rolling out automation that helps shift traffic away from unhealthy regions with safety checks and progressive rollout.”
- DO: “In some cases you may still observe transient errors/latency during instability; we’re focused on reducing duration and frequency of customer-visible impact.”
- DON’T: “Automatic failover guarantees no downtime.”
- DON’T: “Failover happens within X seconds” (unless SRE approves a vetted, range-based statement).

Inputs / links (to be attached in ticket)
- Confluence: controlled failover comms template (oncall/status-page-and-comms)
- Confluence: automated region failover runbook (oncall/runbooks)
- Incident reviews: trigger gaps + lessons learned

Acceptance criteria
- 1-pager + FAQ reviewed and approved by SRE + Platform leads (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes; Mina Haddad or Ethan Park) and Support lead (Dev Patel).
- Support macros updated and shipped to Support ops (Zendesk/Jira macros or internal macro doc) with clear “when to use” guidance.
- Escalation guidance documented: required fields for customer reports + triage decision tree.
- Internal enablement post sent and linked in the runbook/comms template.

Open questions
- Notification expectations: for controlled tests, do we proactively notify all customers or only impacted tiers/routes?
- Dedicated vs Hosted language: what’s the safest baseline statement that covers both without confusing customers?
- Private deployments: what wording is accurate (feature availability varies) while still reassuring enterprise buyers?

Risks
- Over-promising reliability improvements may create contractual expectations.
- Under-explaining controlled tests may increase ticket volume during game days.
- Inconsistent language across SRE, Support, and Sales can confuse customers; we need one approved set of statements.

Next steps
1) Draft 1-pager + FAQ v1 (Marissa) and circulate for review.
2) Working session with Dev Patel + Owen Phillips to validate macro tone and ticket fields.
3) Finalize do/don’t and push enablement note ahead of next production controlled failover window.
comments: 2025-02-20 (Marissa Cole): Draft outline started. Biggest risk is wording around “automatic failover” — propose we say “progressive, safety-guarded traffic shifting” and avoid guarantees on timing/coverage.

2025-02-21 (Dev Patel): Support request: macros must include a short checklist for what to ask customers for (request IDs, timestamps, model, streaming, region) and explicit escalation tags to avoid back-and-forth during incidents.

2025-02-24 (Aisha Bello): Please keep anything about thresholds/hysteresis out of customer docs. OK to say “multiple health signals” and “conservative guardrails.” Also add a line that we may choose degrade-in-place (load shedding/timeouts) before full failover in some cases.
2025-03-03 (Mina Haddad): +1 to “progressive traffic shifting” language. Please add a sentence noting that failover decisions consider capacity in the target region to prevent making things worse.

2025-03-12 (Owen Phillips): Macro request: add an explicit sentence for streaming symptoms (“you may see reconnects / truncated streams”) and recommended customer retry guidance (idempotent retries where possible).

2025-03-28 (Marissa Cole): v1 draft shared for review; awaiting final approvals from SRE + Support before we publish internally. Next: convert macros into Support ops format and link from the controlled test comms template.
